exercise1.prompt: Four questions to ask a new table before you trust a number from it.

hiddenCases.name: a clean file reports nothing missing

exercise1.hint: df.isna().sum() gives a count per column; summing that again gives the total. int() at the end keeps it a plain number.

questions.prompt: Which of these should you check on a table you have just loaded?
questions.explain: Those three answer "is this what I think it is". Permissions are a different problem and the read already succeeded.

choices: A count of missing values per column
questions.explain: isna is a table of masks and summing collapses each column, so you see which column has the gaps rather than just how many there are.

questions.prompt: Why look at the distinct values of a category column?
choices: To find stray spellings and unexpected values
questions.explain: "maths", "Maths" and "MATHS" are three categories to a computer and one to you. The set is where that becomes visible.
